# Pass-1 ladder expressed in classes

## Context / Problem
`workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml:62-65` sets `model_ladder` to BARE names
(`claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`). `production_batch_runner.py:87-93`
assigns `model_ladder[0]` to `cfg.model`, and `config.py:333-341` maps the `claude` prefix to provider
`anthropic`. So during a run configured for another provider, the Pass-1 finders still resolve to
DIRECT ANTHROPIC — a split-brain in the pass that does most of the work (MEASURED: 41 of 42 calls on a
real review). `code_review/batch_runner.py:55` has the same shape.

## Approach
Express the ladder as CLASS names (`trivial`, `standard`, `frontier`) rather than model ids, resolved
through the class config at run time. The ladder keeps its meaning — escalate through capability tiers
— and becomes provider-portable by construction rather than by convention.

**Alternative rejected — provider-qualifying the ladder entries in YAML.** Hard-codes one provider into
the gate definition, which is what makes today's ladder non-portable.

## Scope

CORRECTED: the original list omitted the two files this ticket's OWN mechanism and ACs require.
Verified in source at b4b475b04.

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — **REQUIRED, was missing.** `resolve_model` at config.py:362 is
  literally `return step or workflow or cfg.model`. The MECHANISM section below names this as "the
  ONE funnel", so the reserved-word resolution lands here. Its only caller is
  `workflow/runs.py:154`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py` — **REQUIRED, was missing.** `models_at_or_above` is
  defined at sizing.py:312 and is the subject of the AC about a BEDROCK primary returning
  Bedrock escalation targets. Callers: `prerequisites.py:257`, `sizing.py:371`, and an alias at
  `orchestrator.py:72`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` — the ladder entries. MEASURED: lines 62-65
  currently hold the literal ladder `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` / `claude-opus-4-8`,
  which is what the `grep -n "claude-"` AC targets.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/production_batch_runner.py` and
  `src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py` — resolve a class name to a model.
- `tests/unit/` — resolution and no-cross-provider tests.

### The resolver ALREADY EXISTS — this ticket wires it, it does not build it

`model_classes.resolve_model_string` is delivered and tested by f844: `test_model_classes.py:329`
asserts `resolve_model_string("standard") == "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"` and :342
asserts a literal id round-trips unchanged. So this ticket's job is to route `resolve_model` and
the ladder THROUGH that existing function, not to reimplement class resolution.

### Existing couplings to keep green (measured, so nobody assumes zero)

- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_model_log.py:43` does
  `monkeypatch.setattr(sizing, "models_at_or_above", ...)`. A rebind target: if this ticket moves
  or renames that function, re-importing it elsewhere will NOT fix that patch.
- `orchestrator.py:72` holds `_models_at_or_above = sizing.models_at_or_above`, a module-level
  ALIAS bound at import time, and `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1145,1150` assert through it
  with LITERAL ids. Those must keep returning the same bare ids byte-for-byte — the plan's
  "a literal id keeps working byte-for-byte" guarantee is what makes them safe.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_scoped_ticket_tool.py::test_resolve_model_precedence` pins
  `resolve_model`'s step > workflow > config precedence. Adding class resolution must not disturb
  the precedence ORDER; it resolves the WINNER after precedence is applied.

## Testing
Contract tier: the observable is the model id the batch runner assigns to `cfg.model`.
- a ladder of class names resolves to the configured models, in order.
- with classes configured for a non-default provider, the entry rung does NOT resolve to an
  anthropic-inferred bare id (the split-brain regression).
- the escalation order is unchanged.


## MECHANISM (decided on parent eb58 — do not re-derive)

**A workflow step names a class by using the class name as its `model:` value.** The three class
names are RESERVED VALUES in the EXISTING model-string space. There is no new `class:` key and no
schema change — the v3 step schema stays closed; its VALUE space gains three reserved words.

    model: standard                                  # instead of: model: claude-sonnet-4-6
    model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]      # instead of three literal ids

Resolution happens at the ONE funnel every step model already passes through:
`config.resolve_model(cfg, step=, workflow=)` (`config.py:347`), today literally
`return step or workflow or cfg.model`. If the resolved string is one of `trivial`/`standard`/
`frontier`, resolve it via `model_classes.load_class_slots()`; otherwise return it unchanged. A
literal id keeps working byte-for-byte, so every existing workflow YAML is unaffected and migration
is opt-in per step.

REJECTED — a new `class:` key: forks a step schema `runs.py` documents as closed, forces every
consumer to handle two mutually exclusive keys, and makes `model: standard` vs `class: standard` a
silent ambiguity. Reserved values keep ONE resolution path.

REJECTED — resolving at YAML load time: the class -> id mapping depends on process-scoped env/CLI
layers, so load-time resolution would freeze the wrong value in a long-lived process and would be
invisible to `provider_provenance` (343b).


## The escalation ladder is a SECOND split-brain (measured)

`sizing.MODEL_LADDER` (`sizing.py:99-103`) hardcodes the three BARE Anthropic ids with their context
windows, and `models_at_or_above()` (`sizing.py:312`) returns those bare names for runtime
escalation. Its lookup is a SUBSTRING match, so it happens to match a Bedrock id — but it RETURNS
the bare Anthropic name. MEASURED:

    models_at_or_above("bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6")
      -> [("claude-sonnet-4-6", "anthropic"), ("claude-opus-4-8", "anthropic")]

So a Bedrock run that hits a context limit silently escalates to DIRECT ANTHROPIC: a hard failure in
a Bedrock-only container with no key, or silent Anthropic billing where a key exists. This is
DISTINCT from the entry-rung split-brain this ticket already names (`model_ladder[0]` -> `cfg.model`)
and must be fixed in the same change, or the cutover leaks cross-provider on every escalation.

The ladder's rungs become CLASS names resolved through the same funnel, so escalation stays within
the configured provider for each class.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-1 entry rung resolves through the class config, not a bare model id
- [ ] a test asserts no ladder rung resolves to provider `anthropic` when classes are configured for
      another provider
- [ ] a test asserts the ladder's escalation ORDER is unchanged by the change
- [ ] `grep -n "claude-" src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/plan-review.yaml` returns no model_ladder entry

- [ ] a test asserts `model_ladder: [trivial, standard, frontier]` in a workflow resolves each rung
      through the class config, and that a ladder of literal ids still resolves to those ids unchanged
- [ ] a test asserts `models_at_or_above()` on a BEDROCK primary returns escalation targets that stay
      on BEDROCK — it currently returns bare Anthropic ids that infer to provider `anthropic`, so
      this criterion fails against the current implementation and cannot pass vacuously
- [ ] a test asserts the Pass-1 entry rung comes from the class config rather than
      `model_ladder[0]` being copied into `cfg.model` by the batch runners
